title: Govt issues strict guidelines for Vesak celebrations
byline: The government has issued a new circular to regulate all programmes organised for the upcoming Vesak season, including Vesak zones and Dansals, with authorities banning activities considered inappropriate for the religious festival.

title: Tamil Nadu tourist killed after getting caught in tussle between two elephants
byline: A 33-year-old tourist from Tamil Nadu died after getting caught in a tussle between two captive elephants at Dubare Elephant Camp in Kodagu district on Monday, officials said.

title: Large number of vehicles to be purchased for Wildlife Department: Minister
byline: The tender process has begun to purchase a fleet of 16 double cabs, 84 other cabs and 181 motorbikes for the Department of Wildlife, Minister of Environment Dhammika Patabendi told Parliament today.

title: The best interest of the child must remain our only priority
byline: The ongoing case involving the alleged sexual abuse of a child has caused significant public concern across Sri Lanka.

title: President to lead National War Heroes Commemoration ceremony
byline: The 17th National War Heroes Commemoration ceremony to honor military personnel who sacrificed their lives to liberate the motherland from decades of terrorism, is scheduled to commence today at 3:00 PM at the Ranaviru Memorial in Battaramulla under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: Two clauses of Financial Transaction Reporting Amendment Bill inconsistent with Constitution
byline: The Supreme Court has held that Clauses 22 and 34 of the Financial Transaction Reporting Bill is inconsistent with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne told Parliament today.

title: Musk loses OpenAI court battle after jury finds he waited too long to sue
byline: A California jury has tossed out Elon Musk’s high-profile lawsuit against OpenAI and its boss Sam Altman.

title: Sri Lanka remains undivided because of the Armed Forces: Mahinda Rajapaksa
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa said yesterday that, because of the ultimate sacrifices made by the armed forces, the nation remains a single, undivided country.

title: Wire traps laid to rob motorcyclists; gang nabbed by residents
byline: A gang that allegedly laid wire traps across roads and robbed motorcyclists of their cash and jewellery at Boraketiiya on the Padukka-Wataraka-Boraketiiya Road was caught by residents and handed over to the Meegoda Police in the early hours of yesterday morning.

title: CIABOC official pushing suspects towards suicide: Opposition
byline: Taking a swipe at the Government over the death of former Srilankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Kapila Chandrasena , the joint Opposition yesterday alleged that a certain official of the Commission to Investigate Allegations on Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) was pushing those summoned before the Commission towards suicide.

title: Health experts warn of waterborne disease risk
byline: Health experts have warned of a possible rise in waterborne diseases in the coming weeks as floodwaters from minor flooding in several affected areas begins to recede under the prevailing rainy conditions.

title: Rupee value slides against major currencies
byline: In the wake of the Sri Lankan rupee depreciating rapidly against major international currencies, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said the exchange rate decline could not be used as the sole criterion to determine the status of the economy, as it had both positive and negative implications.

title: Trump says he called off new Iran attack at request of Gulf states
byline: US President Donald Trump has said he is holding off a military attack on Iran planned for Tuesday at the request of Gulf states as ’’serious negotiations are now taking place’’.

title: Without war end, President couldn’t freely visit Jaffna: Namal
byline: National Organiser of the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna Namal Rajapaksa has criticised the government, stating that if war heroes had not ended the war, the current President would not have been able to freely visit Jaffna, but would instead have had to seek permission before doing so.

title: Global recognition for Sri Lanka’s HIV, syphilis elimination efforts
byline: Sri Lanka has been awarded special recognition by the World Health Organization (WHO) for maintaining the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis as a public health concern, in accordance with international standards and global advisory guidelines.

title: Minister’s daughter residing in house belonging to Diaspora member in UK: Chamara
byline: The daughter of a Minister who is engaged in higher studies in the UK is currently lodging in a house belonging to a member of the Tamil diaspora, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake alleged in Parliament.

title: Rough seas and strong winds expected around island
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned that rough seas and strong winds are expected in several sea areas around the island during the next 24 hours.

title: No political authority invited to attend Victory Day celebration: Vijitha
byline: The government said today that no political authority except for the President, Deputy Defence Minister and Deputy Minister of Public Security will attend the Victory Day celebrations today.

title: All Vesak dansals must be registered with MOH offices: Health chief
byline: All Dansals organised across the island for the Vesak festival must be registered with the relevant area Medical Officer of Health (MOH), Health Services Director General, Specialist Dr. Asela Gunawardena said.

title: US drops fraud charges after billionaire Adani pledges $10bn investment
byline: The administration of United States President Donald Trump has moved to dismiss criminal fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani in a case where he is accused of bribing Indian officials for as much as $265m to secure contracts and lying to US investors to land a solar energy project in India, allegations that his company has long denied.

title: One spot, five teams: IPL 2026 Playoff Battle Intensifies
byline: The IPL 2026 league stage is nearing its conclusion, with three teams already securing playoff qualification.

title: Police seek public help to arrest suspect in Thalangama double murder
byline: Police is seeking assistance to arrest a key suspect linked to the brutal shooting of a lawyer and his wife in Thalangama.

title: No reason to increase prices of vehicles imported before May 16: Vijitha
byline: There is no reason to increase the prices of vehicles imported before May 16 as the 50 percent surcharge is not applicable to vehicles imported before May 16, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said today.

title: No one waged war against Tamil community
byline: No one waged war against the Tamil community but only against the LTTE, SLPP MP Namal Rajapaksa told Parliament today.

title: Dengue cases near 30,000 as death toll rises to 15 this year
byline: A total of 29,589 dengue cases and 15 deaths have been reported in Sri Lanka as of May 18 this year, the National Dengue Control Unit said.

title: Cabinet approves potato purchasing programme for farmers
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to purchase 1,000 kilograms of potatoes from each potato farmer through the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE).

title: Indian Air Force Chief arrives in Sri Lanka on official visit
byline: The Chief of the Indian Air Force, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, arrived in Sri Lanka last night (18) on a three-day official visit. He will remain in the country until 21 May.

title: Sri Lanka sets Guinness World Record for sensory board
byline: Sri Lanka has officially secured a Guinness World Record for the world’s longest sensory board at Merak 2026.

title: Water tariffs to stay unchanged
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to maintain existing water supply tariffs without any increase during the first six months of this year.

title: SLC rejects claims of financial crisis
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has rejected media reports claiming that the organization is facing a “financial crisis” following the appointment of the Cricket Transformation Committee.

title: Ravi raises alarm over cyber vulnerabilities in banks, State institutions
byline: UNP MP Ravi Karunanayake raised serious concerns in Parliament over the growing vulnerability of Sri Lanka’s public institutions and financial systems to cybercrime, cyberattacks, hacking, ransomware, data breaches and digital espionage.

title: Rupee slides as US Dollar surpasses Rs. 338 mark
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee has weakened further against the US Dollar, with the selling rate surpassing the Rs. 338 mark, according to the latest exchange rate report issued by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka today (19).

title: Five dead, including two teen suspects, after shooting at San Diego mosque
byline: Two teenage gunmen opened fire on Monday at the Islamic Center of San Diego, ​California, killing a security guard and two other men outside the mosque before the suspects were found dead, apparently from self-inflicted gunshot wounds, police said.

title: SJB pays tribute to MR, SF for war victory
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MPs in Parliament today paid tribute to former President Mahinda Rajapaksa and former Sri Lanka Army Commander Sarath Fonseka for the war victory gained 17 years ago.

title: Three arrested with venison and antelope meat in Embilipitiya raid
byline: Three persons were arrested during a surprise raid conducted at a private restaurant in the Padalangala area of Embilipitiya for allegedly displaying, possessing and selling the meat of protected wild animals.

title: Sri Lanka, Russia sign MoU to strengthen railway cooperation
byline: A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between Sri Lanka and Russia to enhance technical and investment cooperation aimed at improving Sri Lanka’s railway services.

title: Over 178,000 vehicles imported within four months this year: Deputy Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando revealed that a total of 178,000 vehicles have been imported by the end of April this year.

title: Court questions absence of statements from two crucial witnesses in Kapila case
byline: The Colombo Fort Magistrate today questioned the absence of statements from two crucial witnesses connected to the death of former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena.

title: Sri Lanka invites global investors for green hydrogen, ammonia projects
byline: Sri Lanka has launched an ambitious drive to attract global investment into the development of green hydrogen and green ammonia projects, with authorities aiming to position the country as a regional hub for clean energy production and exports.

title: Farmers to receive Up to Rs. 100,000 per hectare for Yala crop damage
byline: The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board has announced that farmers will receive compensation of up to Rs. 100,000 per hectare for crop damage caused by recent heavy rains during the ongoing Yala season.

title: Court orders banks, telecom firms to submit details in Hemarathana Thera case
byline: Siyapath Sasindu Wickremeratne, on a report submitted by the Sri Lanka Police, today ordered all state and private banks in the country to individually furnish reports on bank accounts maintained by the mother of the underaged girl allegedly raped by Ven. Pallegama Hemarathana Thera.

title: Inter-agency training push launched to strengthen action against forced labour
byline: A coordinated capacity-building initiative aimed at strengthening national action against forced labour got underway yesterday (18) with the launch of a three-day workshop at the National Plantation Management Institute in Athurugiriya.

title: Government wants media reports kept out of Parliament after Daily Mirror article creates stir
byline: A Daily Mirror report on May 19 titled ‘Rupee value slides against major currencies’ created a debate in Parliament with a question whether Members of Parliament (MPs) should make  comments on what is published by the media.

title: Sri Lanka targets fourfold increase in honey production
byline: The Agriculture Department has launched a special programme aimed at increasing Sri Lanka’s annual honey production from 50 metric tons to 200 metric tons, Director General of Agriculture Dr. Thushara Wickramarachchi said.

title: No gender-change procedures on children: Castle Street Hospital
byline: Castle Street Hospital for Women has denied allegations circulating on social media claiming that gender-change procedures are being performed on children at the hospital.

title: School for the deaf conquers new frontier, basketball
byline: For the students of the Ratmalana School for the Deaf, “Forward Beyond Barriers” is no longer just a school motto, but a reality lived and shared on the basketball court. Gaining the attention of a wider audience, the school’s basketball team recently competed for the first time ever in the Schools Basketball Tournament 2026 Division D - Tier 2 boys’ competition, marking an important milestone for student-athletes with disabilities.

title: American who contracted Ebola in DR Congo evacuated for treatment
byline: An American tested positive for Ebola after being exposed while working with a medical missionary group in the Democratic Republic of Congo, US officials say.

title: Early rally fades as profit-taking reverses gains amid geopolitical uncertainty
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange started today’s session on a strong positive note, supported by news of a potential peace deal between Iran and the USA. The ASPI surged by more than 240 points within the first 15 minutes of trading, reflecting strong early optimism and broad-based buying interest across the market.

title: Vehicle number plate printing to commence by June 10 under new contract: DMT
byline: The printing of vehicle number plates in Sri Lanka is scheduled to officially commence on or before June 10, 2026, under the terms of the newly awarded contract, Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) Acting Commissioner General K.P.N.T.N. Devapriya said.

title: President vows to fulfil war heroes’ dream
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake today said the aspirations of the country’s war heroes extended beyond defeating terrorism and included building a developed, peaceful and just nation for future generations.

title: Southwest monsoon gradually establishing over Sri Lanka: Met Dept.
byline: The Meteorology Department says the southwest monsoon is gradually getting established over the island.

title: Parliament approves Inland Revenue Amendment Bill
byline: The Inland Revenue Amendment Bill was approved by Parliament with amendments today.

title: Russia conducts major nuclear drills
byline: Russia on Tuesday begins three days of nuclear drills ​that will include the ​launch of ballistic and cruise missiles, ⁠the defence ministry said.

title: Sri Lanka envoy presents credentials to Malaysian King Sultan Ibrahim
byline: Sri Lanka’s High Commissioner to Malaysia, Dharshana M. Perera, presented his Letter of Credence to His Majesty King Sultan Ibrahim at a ceremonial event held yesterday (18) at the Istana Negara (Royal Palace) in Kuala Lumpur.

title: Teachers’ Union questions appointment to education reform panel due to allegations
byline: The Ceylon Teachers’ Union (CTU) has called for an immediate investigation into the appointment of Acting Director of the Meepe Educational Leadership and Development Centre, Dumina Lellopitiya, to a sub-committee under the National Steering Committee for Education Reforms.

title: Ashu Marasinghe defamation case settled in court
byline: Former Parliamentarian Prof. Ashu Marasinghe’s defamation case seeking Rs.1.5 billion in compensation from former Parliamentarian Hirunika Premachandra and another respondent over an alleged statement that he abused a dog was settled before the Kaduwela Magistrate’s Court yesterday after the parties reached a compromise.
